confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer anchors on crowdsourced cost-of-living figures from MyLifeElsewhere and TravelTables. The two sources don't agree, and some TravelTables data is old (last updated July 2023). I adjusted the figures for tourist and beach-area venues and projected them to July 2026. Beer came out at about USD 1.9 to 2.7, coffee at about 2.3 to 3.2, and an inexpensive meal at about 2.3 to 3.2. I raised the meal figure to reflect sit-down restaurants used by visitors. I didn't search directly for cocktail or wine prices. I estimated them from how they usually compare with beer in Kenya and from general knowledge: imported wine and spirits are much more expensive than local beer. These two anchors are less certain. The accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only. I didn't check any booking pages or current listings. July is a busy season on the Kenyan coast, so room rates could vary widely.
comparable_city_reasoning: Main basis is crowdsourced price data for Mombasa itself, cross-checked against Nairobi and Kenyan coastal tourist towns such as Diani and Malindi. On the Kenyan coast, local food is cheap, imported drinks cost much more, and tourist-area hotels charge a premium.
